Requirement: All processing must have lawful basis
Implementation: Legal basis tracked in gdpr_metadata table (consent, contract, legal_obligation, vital_interests, public_task, legitimate_interests)

Requirement: Data only used for stated purposes
Implementation: Purpose field in gdpr_metadata tracks intended use

Requirement: Delete data when no longer needed

Implementation: Public request page /dsar/<booking handle> or a request logged by staff; after email confirmation an expiring JSON export with the processing information is emailed. Free text, message bodies and documents are withheld and counted until the firm reviews them and completes the request
Notes: One calendar month from confirmation. Gaps: conversations and messages not reachable (#1015); email suppressions and bounce receipts not exported (#956)

Implementation: Rectification request is recorded and decided by a firm admin, who corrects the lead or contact in the CRM (edits are audit logged). The system does not change the data itself

Admin-approved erasure runs in one transaction and anonymises the CRM core in place (leads, contacts, notes, activities, booker fields, embeddings, search vectors) and deletes AI scores and insights. Emails, tickets, chats, feedback, notifications, drafts and stored files are a counted checklist cleared by hand
Notes: Replaces anonymize_record(), which was never applied. Gaps: checklist not stored (#1009); AI-created tasks keep text (#1010); conversations and messages (#1015); email suppressions and bounce receipts (#956); no legal hold register, so the admin confirms none applies

Implementation: A per-firm processing restriction keyed on the normalised email stops AI scoring, embeddings, drafts, insights, predictions and the other AI paths that send the person's data to a model; lead and contact pages show a banner; an admin lifts it after telling the person
Notes: Outreach and marketing are not stopped automatically. Replaces the unapplied legal_holds table. A rejected restriction can survive an address change (#1007)

Implementation: Access and portability requests share one JSON export (structured, machine-readable) emailed as an expiring link
Notes: JSON only. No CSV and no direct transfer to another controller (Art 20(2)); follow-up task not yet filed

Implementation: An objection request creates a processing restriction on completion. A marketing objection also needs the admin to confirm marketing has stopped and say how
Notes: Marketing is not stopped automatically (outreach suppression follow-up task not yet filed).

Implementation: Incident response plan with breach notification
Consents table tracks consent with audit trail
AI scores include confidence + human override

Public requests are confirmed through a single-use emailed link (24 hours, 32 random bytes, stored only as a keyed hash, compared in constant time). Staff-logged requests record how identity was checked and a note of at least 20 characters; a staff-logged erasure needs a second admin or a 24 hour pause
Notes: Email ownership is the check for public requests

Implementation: Retention by classification: PUBLIC(7y), INTERNAL(3y), CONFIDENTIAL(10y), PRIVILEGED(permanent)

Erasure replaces personal fields in place: the email becomes erased-<row id>@erased.invalid, names and contact fields are cleared, embeddings and search vectors are cleared; database triggers stop an erased record being written back
Notes: Replaces anonymize_record(), which was never applied. Communications stay until the admin clears them. Erased data remains in encrypted backups until they expire

Requirement: Log all data access and changes

Implementation: Deadline is one calendar month from confirmation (staff-logged: from the date received), one extension of 1 or 2 months with a reason emailed to the person. A job emails firm admins 7 days before the deadline and every 3 days while overdue
Notes: A failed completion or refusal email is not retried (#1014)
